Subject: Re: CedarBank RFP — Vulnerability management questionnaire (technical clarifications)

Team — adding more detail for the questionnaire so Neha has what she needs to populate the workbook. Key points to include in answers:

1) SAST / DAST
- We run SAST during PR gates with a configurable policy; typical cadence is on every merge to main and daily scheduled scans for release branches.
- DAST is run against staging/prefinal environments with authenticated scan support; scheduling typically prior to production pushes and for quarterly full-app sweeps.
- False positives: triage workflow integrates with Jira; standard triage SLA is 3 business days to label/confirm.

2) Patch SLAs and emergency response
- Severity mapping: Critical (CVSS >=9.0) — emergency response within 24 hours; High — remediation window 7 days; Medium/Low — 30/90 days respectively.
- Emergency hotpatching: our runtime supports blue/green and can deploy hotfixes with 4-hour rollback capability; we also have canary gates tied to tracing/latency metrics.

3) Pen testing and evidence
- Annual third-party penetration tests; we can provide redacted executive summaries and a scoped findings register. Vendors: RedTeam Labs (2025) — see attached summary.

4) SBOM
- SBOM generated at build time (CycloneDX format). We include direct and transitive dependencies for all public language ecosystems used in our base images. For runtime-managed model artifacts we provide a manifest of model runtime libs and build-time tool versions.

Attachments referenced for submission: pen-test-summary-2025.pdf, sbom-manifest-2026-02.json. I'll prepare short answers for the workbook cells and mark anything that needs CISO/legal sign-off.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Applied Security — Redwood Inference

- For the Patch SLA: can you provide an example runbook for a Critical CVE (timeline and stakeholders) and whether Redwood will provide temporary mitigations if a customer cannot accept a hotpatch immediately?

Procurement also asked for a short executive one-pager that summarizes risk posture and evidence we can attach to our vendor risk system (CedarBank-Vendor-Risk). If you can send those items by EOD 2026-02-18 we'll review them internally.

Also happy to take the 30-minute call — propose Tue 17 Feb 10:00am ET, but open to another slot.

Regards,

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: CedarBank RFP — Vulnerability management questionnaire (executive summary + deliverables)

Amir — attaching the requested artifacts: a one-page executive summary and the completed questionnaire workbook. Highlights included in the exec summary:

- Coverage: SAST (PR gates + scheduled scans), DAST (auth scans in staging + quarterly sweeps), and annual third-party pen tests.
- SBOM: CycloneDX manifests produced at build time; includes both language package managers and OS-level/transitive dependencies for our base images. For model bundles we provide an SBOM-like manifest enumerating runtime libs and toolchain versions.
- Patch SLA: Critical CVE response timeline — detection/triage (0–8 hrs), emergency patch dev & test (8–24 hrs), staged rollout (24–48 hrs). If a customer cannot accept an immediate hotpatch, we provide mitigations (traffic filters, WAF rules, temporary config changes) documented in the runbook and we work with the customer on compensating controls until patching is possible.

Attachments: redwood_exec_summary_cedarbank.docx, completed_vm_questionnaire.xlsx

I've also pasted a short runbook excerpt below for immediate use. If you want the full runbook and redacted pen-test register we can surface that under NDA.

--- runbook excerpt ---
1) Detection/Triage (0–8 hrs): Internal alerting triggered -> security on-call notified -> preliminary impact assessment.
2) Containment (8–12 hrs): Temporary mitigations (config lock, remove vulnerable feature flags, WAF rules).
3) Remediation (12–48 hrs): Backport/patch, CI verification, canary deploys with health checks.
4) Post-incident (48–120 hrs): Root cause analysis, customer notification, disclosure artifacts.

Let us know if Tuesday 17 Feb at 10:00am ET still works for a short call — we'll book the slot if accepted.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Director — Redwood Inference
